Round 4 market, prices start at 12. Sell 3 for cash = 31m cash, strong. But next round cash devalues 62%, promissory survives. Last round is 6; round 5 market still one more market. Prices reset? sold_counter resets to 0 each round apparently. Selling credit gives promissory 38.75m paid at end without devaluation—but promissory after last round not redeemed. Round 4 promissory is paid at round 5 start (added to cash), then round 6 start devalued? Cash at start of round 6 = floor(cash/100)*62, promissory added after. So promissory from round 4 market → added round 5, devalued round 6 start. Hmm.

Actually cash devaluation applies at start of round 5 to cash held. Sell now gets 31m cash which will be devalued to 62% next round. Sell credit gets 38.75m promissory added round 5 without devaluation... but then at round 6 start it's part of cash and devalued again? Round 6: cash=floor(cash/100)*62, promissory added after. So credit sell avoids one devaluation round (round 5's). So credit sell is better: 38.75 vs 31*... wait selling cash gives 31m at round 4, devalued to 19.2m at round 5. Credit 38.75m paid round 5 no devaluation. Then round 6 both devalued equally? Credit: 38.75→ at r6 start 24m cash. Cash: 31→19.2m at r5, then at r6 11.9m. So sell_credit 3 is better.

But we might sell more in round 5-6 markets; selling now moves counter. Also could sell fewer now and more later. Prices reset per round? sold_counter 0 at round 4 market, so each round prices start fresh. Selling 3 now at credit: 12+10+9=31*1.25=38.75. Then round 5 sell remaining goods. Fine. Choose 6.
